title: Computational Framework for Identifying Ion Channel Mutation-Compensating Interventions
inspection_scope: Primary PDF read directly; metadata checked on page 1, model/method discussion on page 6 and Kv7.2 results/figures on pages 13–15. Page 15 (Figure 7) inspected visually. No simulation or implementation audit.
main_text_placement: 8.1 Biological relevance of the reconstruction boundary
supported_comparison: In the Kv7.2 D212G model, changing sodium, delayed-rectifier potassium and leak conductances reduces a reference spike-count discrepancy while the mutated M-current remains unchanged. This is compensation of a measured function in the treated model, complementary to record-based reconstruction across replacement.
interpretive_limits: No validation of a treatment in living systems is inferred.
A spike-count comparison does not establish equivalence under every challenge.
Persistence after withdrawal and autonomous maintenance are not established by this compensation result.
This study supplies no evidence here for acquired-record renewal or transmission across fresh-body replacement.
The new paragraph uses the explicit Kv7.2 case and makes no all-other-channels-only claim for R859C.
